name: Fault-equivalent 2n-legged spider ladder
summary: A 2n-legged Z-spider is fault-equivalent to two n-legged spiders whose legs are connected pairwise.
description:
A phase-free Z-spider with $2n$ legs is fault-equivalent to two $n$-legged spiders, each of whose legs passes through a three-legged spider, with the $i$-th three-legged spider of the one connected to the $i$-th three-legged spider of the other. The rungs form detecting regions, so that flips which would spread to many legs are detected. Fault equivalence is with respect to *edge-flip noise*: every edge of the diagram can suffer a Pauli $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ flip of weight 1.

This is the form of the even spider decomposition used in *Fault Tolerance by Construction*; it is the [distance-preserving decomposition of an even spider](../fe-even-spider-decomposition/) with each four-legged spider split into two connected three-legged ones. If only $w$-fault equivalence is required, fewer rungs suffice: see the [w-fault-equivalent version](../fe-fuse-n-w/).

source.location: Sec. 6.2, rule $(\textsc{Fuse-n}_{\text{fe}})$; proof in the appendix

parameter_notes: A spider with 2n legs (shown for n = 3); holds for any n ≥ 1.
